data.text/markdown:
00 — Convert CellProfiler output to Parquet (CytoTable)

Pipeline step: 0 (first step) Position in pipeline: CellProfiler output → NB00 (convert to Parquet) → NB01 (data QC) Purpose: turn the raw CellProfiler output into one Parquet file per plate (or per input) with one row per cell, using CytoTable.
This notebook converts only. It never edits the raw files and does no QC, normalisation or renaming of columns. Data QC is NB01.
Input: workspace/backend/<EXPERIMENT_ID>/, one of:
What is in the folder Output
CellProfiler SQLite database(s), one per plate one Parquet per database, named after it
The four tables Per_Image.csv, Per_Cells.csv, Per_Cytoplasm.csv, Per_Nuclei.csv one Parquet, named after the experiment
One merged single-cell CSV one Parquet, named after the CSV
Outputs:
  • analysis/<EXPERIMENT_ID>/outputs/parquet/<name>.parquet — read by NB01
  • analysis/<EXPERIMENT_ID>/results/parquet_conversion/conversion_summary.csv, input_checks.csv, provenance_nb00_latest.json

Execution logic

  1. Choose the experiment; set overwrite, threads and chunk size if needed.
  2. Find the raw input and list what will be converted.
  3. Convert with CytoTable (existing Parquet is kept unless overwrite is on).
  4. Check the Parquet files: what NB01 will find, and whether cells are unique.
  5. Write the summary tables and provenance; run integrity checks.
0 — Imports and shared utilities

data.text/markdown:
1 — Experiment configuration

Pick the experiment folder under workspace/backend/. Overwrite, threads and chunk size are the only settings.
  • Overwrite: an existing Parquet file is kept unless this is on. If the raw file is newer than the Parquet file, section 3 warns you to turn it on.
  • Threads, chunk size (under Advanced): CytoTable reads each table in chunks of this many rows. The defaults suit most plates; raise the chunk size for very large tables if memory allows.

data.text/markdown:
2 — Find the raw input

SQLite databases win over CSV files. CSV files must be the four Per_* tables or exactly one merged CSV; any other mix is refused, because converting unrelated CSV files together would mix their columns. A merged CSV needs a numeric ImageNumber column (CellProfiler writes it) so it can be read in chunks.

data.text/markdown:
3 — Convert with CytoTable

What: each input becomes one Parquet file with one row per cell. For SQLite and Per_* tables, CytoTable reads Image, Cells, Cytoplasm and Nuclei in chunks and joins them. A cell is kept when its cytoplasm object has a parent cell, a parent nucleus and an image (the same rule as the readers NB04 uses). A merged CSV is converted as it is. Reason: Parquet is typed and columnar, so NB01 can read only the few hundred columns QC needs instead of the whole table, and it does so in seconds. CytoTable does the chunked reading and the join for CellProfiler's table layout. Choices made here:
  • CytoTable's built-in join keeps only Image_FileName_* from the image table. Data QC also needs Image_ImageQuality_* (blur, saturation), Image_PathName_* and Image_Count_*, so the join here keeps every image column.
  • Column names are not changed (ImageNumber, Image_Metadata_Plate, ...); NB01 applies the usual Plate/Well/Site renaming when it loads.
  • CytoTable runs in threads, not subprocesses (works the same on Windows).
Assumptions: object numbers in the Cells, Nuclei and Cytoplasm tables are unique within an image, and every database or table set holds whole plates (cells of one plate are not split across inputs).

data.text/markdown:
4 — Check the Parquet files: what NB01 will find

Question: can the data-QC notebook use these files as they are? Each check reads only the Parquet footers or a handful of columns.
Result Meaning
PASS NB01 finds what it needs
WARN NB01 runs with less: it falls back or skips a figure
FAIL NB01 will stop; fix the input or the CellProfiler pipeline first
The most important check is that every cell is unique by plate, well, site, image and object number. If two plates share a Metadata_Plate value (for example two folders that are both called …_Plate_1), their cells collide, and QC flags would be attached to the wrong cells.

5 — Write the summary tables

File Rows Used by
conversion_summary.csv one per input: raw files, raw cells, Parquet file, cells, columns review
input_checks.csv the checks of section 4 review
The summary holds only values that do not change between runs (no timings), so a rerun without overwrite does not fail on a harmless difference. Existing files are protected: a file whose content differs is not replaced unless Overwrite existing outputs is on.

data.text/markdown:
Notebook complete

This notebook converted the raw CellProfiler output to Parquet, without changing any raw file or any column name:
  1. Found the input (SQLite, Per_* CSV tables or one merged CSV).
  2. Converted it with CytoTable to one row per cell, keeping all image columns.
  3. Checked that NB01 will find its columns and that every cell is unique.
It did not do QC, normalise values or remove cells. Next: open NB01 (data QC).

Key outputs

  • analysis/<EXPERIMENT_ID>/outputs/parquet/*.parquet — one row per cell; read by NB01
  • results/parquet_conversion/conversion_summary.csv — raw vs. converted cells per input
  • results/parquet_conversion/input_checks.csv — what NB01 will find (PASS / WARN / FAIL)
  • results/parquet_conversion/provenance_nb00_latest.json — run provenance

Save the analysis record

Save the notebook's current session without rerunning cells:
  • HTML preserves code and the complete rich-output record;
  • PDF provides a clean reading copy without code inputs.
Chromium can write both files directly to the experiment's reports/ folder after authorization. Safari shows separate HTML and PDF download buttons because it cannot write directly to a selected folder.
